text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
RANDOLPH CHURCHILL, Father of WINSTON, was born in 1849.
Russian opera singer FEODOR CHALIAPIN was born on this day in 1873.
Belgian crime novelist GEORGES SIMENON, creator of "MAIGRET", was born in 1903.
American film actor and star of many comedies, GEORGE SEGAL, was born in 1934. His films included "A Touch Of Class" with GLENDA JACKSON.

US singer and guitarist PETER TORK, who became a member of the Monkees in 1965, was born in 1944. He was the first to leave the group in 1968 and had to pay $160,000 to buy out his contract. In 1981 he toured Japan with his new band 'New Monks'. He had several unsuccessful projects and worked as a waiter. He and MICKY DOLENZ and DAVID JONES regrouped in 1986 and had a hit with "That Was Then, This Is Now".

British rock musician PETER GABRIEL, former member of the band 'GENESIS', was born on this day in 1950. After leaving the band he produced a number of successful solo albums. Hits included "Solsbury Hill" (1977), "Games Without Frontiers" (1980), "Sledgehammer" (1986) and "Big Time" (1986). He teamed up with KATE BUSH for the successful "Don't Give Up" in 1986.
US bass player with 'Foreigner' EDWARD JOHN GAGLIARDI was born in 1952. He was with the group from 1976 to 1979. In 1982 he appeared with the group 'Spys'. No text received
** EVENTS **
1542 : CATHERINE HOWARD, fifth wife of King HENRY VIII
of England, was executed for adultery.
1689 : WILLIAM of Orange and his wife MARY, daughter of
the deposed JAMES II, were declared joint sovereigns of Great Britain and Ireland.
1692 : JOHN CAMPBELL, at the head of an English force,
led the Glencoe massacre against the Macdonalds in Scotland.
1858 : Sir RICHARD BURTON and Captain JOHN SPEKE became
the first Europeans to discover Lake Tanganyika in East Africa.
1866 : The JAMES YOUNGER gang pulled-off one of the
biggest robberies of the time, stealing 60,000 dollars from a bank in Missouri.
1883 : German composer RICHARD WAGNER died.
1917 : Dutch spy and 'femme fatale' MATA HARI was
arrested by the French.
1929 : Commander HIGGINS took over the Salvation Army
from General BOOTH.
1935 : A jury in New Jersey found BRUNO HAUPTMANN guilty

of kidnapping and murdering the infant son of 'flying ace' CHARLES LINDBERGH 3 years earlier. He was sentenced to death by electric chair. The LINDBERGH's had paid a $50,000 ransom but the baby's body was found two months later. HAUPTMANN was found spending the ransom money and more was found in his cellar.
1941 : Penicillin was used on a human for the first time.
He was a policeman from Oxford in England.
1945 : British and U.S. air force planes bombed Dresden
over 14 hours, killing at least 35,000 people.
1960 : France tested its first atomic bomb in the Sahara
Desert.
1969 : Human eggs, removed from female volunteers, were
fertilised for the first time in a test-tube at England's Cambridge university.
1971 : South Vietnamese troops, aided by United States
forces, entered Laos.
1979 : JEAN RENOIR, French film maker, died. His "Nana",
"La Grande Illusion", "La Bete Humaine", "The Golden Couch" and "Le Regles de Jeux" are masterpieces of cinema.
1991 : An American missile hit an air-raid shelter in
Baghdad, killing at least 300 civilians.
1991 : Germany's "RED ARMY" faction attacked the United
States Embassy in Bonn.
